Found during LB2 (iteration 19), a genuine open design question rather than a bug I could fix unilaterally: `POST /jobs/{job_id}/archive` (design D16-D18, `hub/hub/api/v1/jobs.py`) does not require a job's `Loop`, if it has one, to have already ended (`ending_state` set) before the JOB can be archived — only `POST /loops/{loop_id}/archive` enforces that. So an agent or operator can archive a bare job whose loop is still actively firing, which hides that loop from the default job listing (`job.loop` is only visible through `GET /jobs`/`GET /jobs/{id}`) while it keeps running unattended in the background — arguably the exact governance failure D17 states as the reason a *running loop itself* cannot be archived. I did not add this restriction: D17's own text is explicitly scoped to the loop ('A loop that is running SHALL NOT be archivable'), never extended to a job that owns one, and the task text for B2.2 ('Archive route for a job, and for a loop') does not ask for it either. If you want job-archival to refuse while its loop is still running, that's a small follow-up to `archive_job` in `jobs.py` — say so and it's a quick change.

traps: Do NOT run two pytest invocations concurrently in this repo. Doing so during prep produced a spurious 'no tests ran' AND a spurious '2385 skipped' — either of which reads as a green or as inherited breakage. Run one at a time.
The Bash tool's cwd PERSISTS between calls. A bare `cd hub && ...` after a previous `cd hub` silently resolves wrong. Use absolute paths.
`pytest hub/tests/ tests/` together fails collection. Run them separately.
The full hub suite exceeds the 600s foreground cap — run it in the background or in file chunks.

page-jobs / page-tasks / page-spec do NOT exist in the running app — they are mocks in hub/ui/src/__tests__/App-mount.test.tsx. Grepping hub/ui/src without excluding __tests__ reports 104 test ids; production markup has 71.
Playwright's count() does not auto-wait, and neither do conditional guards. Use expect(...) before acting and assert the post-condition, or you get a false green (this has happened three times here).
PowerShell here-strings (@'...'@) are a syntax error in the Bash tool. Write commit messages to a file and use `git commit -F`.
Remove-Item with a VARIABLE path is blocked by a guard regardless of its value. Literal paths work.
$(pwd) in Git Bash yields /c/Users/... which aiosqlite cannot open. Use the Windows path form.
Launching `agentweave` from a directory containing hub/ silently produces no server (sys.path shadowing). Launch from a neutral cwd.
Git Bash `date` on this machine prints UTC but labels it +0100 — a heartbeat written from it lands an hour in the future and stalls the driver. Stamp timestamps from PowerShell or Python.
Keep any .ps1 ASCII-only. PowerShell 5.1 reads a BOM-less UTF-8 file as ANSI and an em dash breaks quoting.
A writing agent gets an isolated git worktree, so UNTRACKED files in the project directory are invisible to it.
